title: Stop the Scroll in 3 Seconds
subtitle: How a simple hook turns strangers into viewers
intro: You have 3 seconds before someone scrolls past you. How do you make them stop?
takeaway: A hook earns you 3 seconds of attention so your story can earn the rest.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: the shop window
sections.body:
Think of your post like a shop window on a busy street.

People walk fast and look at dozens of windows. A hook is the one bright sign that makes them stop and look inside.

Without it, even a great shop gets ignored. With it, you get a chance to invite them in.

sections.heading: Why it exists: attention you have to earn
sections.body:
A storytelling hook is the first line of your video or post, designed to grab attention instantly.

Templates make this easy. For example: "I didn't plan to talk about this, but pretending (insert situation) was fine wasn't working anymore." You just fill in the blank with your story.

You use it because attention is short. The hook stops the scroll so engagement can start.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when hooks backfire
sections.body:
A hook only works if the story behind it delivers.

If you use a dramatic line like "This looks like a normal moment, but it changed my life completely" and then share something boring, viewers feel tricked and leave.

- Too vague: no one knows what you're talking about
- Too clickbaity: promise is bigger than payoff

Match the hook to a real payoff, or trust breaks.
